trajectory.thought: The leader is a seeded baseline (median of all 19 models) and the runner-up margin is statistically indistinguishable. The stopping rule is clear: when the leader is a seed and the verdict is 'indistinguishable', accepting is the right call. The median's robustness to the 11 weaker models (median error 157, worst 490) is exactly what this trend-dominated, high-spread series needs, and no subset or weighting strategy has beaten it.

action_args.justification: The series is strongly trend-dominated (trend strength 0.93, no seasonality) with a large error spread across 19 models (26.6x). The median of the full pool is the most robust combination: it is insensitive to the 11 models with median error 157 and worst 490, while still benefiting from the top DWT_catboost and ONLY_DWT_catboost models. The runner-up (trimmed_mean of 7 stable models) is not statistically distinguishable, and the weighted meta-model approach scored worse, confirming that robustness beats fitted weights on only 3 validation windows. Accepting the seed baseline is the safest and most defensible choice.

The fact that median of ALL 19 models is the best suggests that the robustness of median is key here - it's not being dragged down by the worst models. The trimmed means of smaller pools are close but not better.
